rationale.correct:
THREE MANDATORY COMMISSIONING STEPS (PD 1096 Rule VII Section 704; ASHRAE 378):

1. REFRIGERANT CHARGE VERIFICATION (Mandatory Step 1)
Test: Weigh actual refrigerant charge in each outdoor unit against manufacturer nameplate specification (per ASHRAE 378 or equivalent blow-down recovery procedure).
Acceptance Criteria: Charge within ±10% of nameplate (e.g., 2.1 kg nameplate ±0.21 kg = 1.89–2.31 kg actual).
Why Critical for Tropical Operation: R-32 in Philippines operates at high ambient (32–34°C). Undercharge (<1.89 kg) reduces cooling capacity and increases compressor discharge temperature, risking oil breakdown and bearing failure in weeks. Overcharge (>2.31 kg) elevates system pressure beyond relief valve settings, risking compressor damage and A2L flammability hazard (charge exceeds PD 1058 Section 7.2 safety limits without secondary containment). Tropical high-humidity (70–90% RH) accelerates refrigerant moisture ingress if system not sealed; charge verification confirms no air/moisture contamination.

2. REFRIGERANT LINESET LEAK TEST (Mandatory Step 2)
Test: Pressure decay test per ASHRAE 378 (pressurize lineset to 1.5× design pressure with dry nitrogen, measure pressure drop over 15 minutes; also acceptable: electronic trace gas detection with ultrasonic or infrared probe at all joints).
Acceptance Criteria: Pressure decay <0.5 bar per minute (equivalent to <3 grams refrigerant loss per year). No leaks detected at joints, coil connections, or vibration-prone bends.
Why Critical for Tropical Operation: Tropical humidity (80% RH) and salt-spray (coastal areas) accelerate copper lineset corrosion externally; internal moisture ingress causes acid formation, sludge buildup, and compressor bearing seizure. 150 m lineset in 6-story tower has ~30–40 joint connections (indoor-to-outdoor runs per floor, distributed lines). A single pinhole leak (0.1 mm) on suction line loses 1–2 kg refrigerant in 6–12 months undetected, gradually degrading cooling; PD 1096 requires pressure test before refrigerant charge to isolate mechanical integrity from thermal/electrical issues.

3. PERFORMANCE RATING TEST (Mandatory Step 3)
Test: Operate system at design conditions (outdoor ambient 33°C ±1°C, indoor 28°C setpoint, 50% loading minimum), measure: (a) Cooling output (BTU/hr, TR), (b) Input power (kW), (c) calculated COP, (d) condensate drain rate (L/hr), (e) compressor discharge temperature, (f) suction line temperature drop at indoor coil (indicates superheat, latent control).
Acceptance Criteria: (1) Cooling output ≥95% of rated capacity; (2) COP ≥3.6 (≥95% of 3.8 nameplate, accounting ±3% measurement variance); (3) Condensate drain functional, measured rate ≥0.5 L/hr (confirms latent capacity); (4) Suction line superheat 8–15°C above dew point (indicates proper latent control, prevents coil freeze at part-load); (5) Compressor discharge <60°C (normal operation; >65°C indicates overcharge or valve issue).
Why Critical for Tropical Operation: Philippine buildings operate in 70–90% RH, 32–34°C ambient continuous. A VRF system undersized by 5–10% in cooling capacity (measured 90% of rated) is masked during commissioning at partial load; once occupied, system struggles in peak load (35°C+ outdoors, high occupancy), cycling continuously, failing to maintain 24°C setpoint or 50–60% RH (mold, condensation risk). Latent control test (superheat measurement, condensate rate verification) is often omitted in Philippine practice but critical in tropical climate; undersized latent capacity (superheat >20°C, drain rate <0.5 L/hr) results in insufficient dehumidification, 70%+ indoor RH, and mold within 3–6 months. Compressor discharge temperature >65°C indicates A2L R-32 system overpressurization (charge/control fault), dangerous in confined spaces (flammability risk per ISO 5149 A2L protocol).

Summary: Charge verification → Lineset leak test → Performance rating test are sequential (logical order): First verify refrigerant integrity (charge weigh-in), confirm system sealed (pressure decay), then validate thermal/latent performance under load. Omitting any step risks: (1) No charge verification: Silent refrigerant loss over months; (2) No leak test: Lineset pinhole discovered after occupancy, water damage; (3) No performance test: Undersized cooling/latent capacity discovered too late, mold/occupant complaints domino effect in tropical climate.

Source: PD 1096 Rule VII Section 704; ASHRAE 378 Refrigerant Leak Detection Standard; LEA-UTIL-002-04 Module Commissioning Checklist.
rationale.takeaway: PD 1096 Rule VII Section 704 and ASHRAE 378 mandatory commissioning for tropical VRF systems: (1) Charge verification (±10% of nameplate) protects against undercharge/overcharge in high-ambient operation; (2) Lineset leak test (pressure decay <0.5 bar/min) ensures system sealed against tropical moisture/corrosion ingress; (3) Performance rating (COP ≥3.6, superheat 8–15°C, drain rate ≥0.5 L/hr) validates latent cooling and dehumidification critical for 70–90% RH Philippines. Omitting any step risks silent refrigerant loss, mold growth, or occupant comfort failure post-handover.
